title: Acquired gamma-root filtering with paid factor pruning and whole-record bounds
statement: For the CIR signal dS=kappa(m nu-S)dt+sqrt(2 kappa nu S)dW with supplied thermal Gamma(m,1/nu) initialization and complete fine aggregate count times of known predictable efficiency c_t in [0,c_max], the gamma-mixture posterior admits a positive Poisson-times-Bernoulli PGF representation. Root interlacing creates at most two new tags per count; each tagged p-factor decays at least e^(-kappa elapsed time). Replacing Bernoulli(p) by Poisson(p) preserves positivity and the represented first moment while paying TV at most p^2. A finite-horizon schedule yields joint count-record/terminal-radius TV <= epsilon with logarithmic expected root count; a separate anytime schedule yields global count-record TV <= epsilon with logarithmically growing expected root count.

requires: Complete aggregate count times, not hidden counts or binary nonempty bins.
Supplied known predictable control 0<=c_t<=c_max and supplied thermal initial Gamma(m, rate 1/nu).
The exact CIR/gamma-mixture class and its parameters are available to the acquired update.
provides: An acquired root-update algorithm using only its own stored parameters and actual aggregate count times.
For fixed horizon T and tau: TV(law(Y_[0,T],S_T),shadow)<=2 c_max m nu T tau^2 and E[M_t]<=2 c_max m nu/kappa log(1/tau), also under true-record input.
With tau=sqrt(epsilon/(2 c_max m nu T)): joint-law error<=epsilon and E[M_t]<=c_max m nu/kappa log(2 c_max m nu T/epsilon).

With the per-tag anytime schedule in the cited source: every finite record/terminal-radius law and the entire count-record law have TV<=epsilon; E[M_t]<=2 c_max m nu/kappa [0.5 log(2 c_max m nu t0/epsilon)+log(1+t/t0)].
assumptions: m,kappa,nu>0; thermal Gamma(m,1/nu) initialization; complete fine count times; one shared predictable control functional in both compared laws.
Reset is a known-state computational approximation Bernoulli(p)->Poisson(p), not a physical reset or unknown-posterior oracle.
Fixed threshold 0<tau<1; finite horizon T>0 and 0<epsilon<2 c_max m nu T when choosing tau from epsilon. The finite-horizon joint-law guarantee is for 0<=t<=T.
Anytime rule: c_max,t0>0 and 0<epsilon<2 c_max m nu t0; each inherited tag keeps its birth threshold. This differs from fixed tau.
Any external long-history controller memory is not included; both laws use the same predictable control functional.
costs: The bounds count expected stored real parameters. Root bracketing, arithmetic, rate integration, event-time precision and numerical likelihood error require separate accounting. Fixed-tau error grows with T; the anytime schedule has log-growing expected state size.
contract.units: m, lambda, p, epsilon and tau are dimensionless; kappa has inverse-time units; S and nu share the chosen scaled-intensity unit and beta has its inverse. c_t S is a count rate, not a probability; c_t need not lie in [0,1].
contract.obstruction: No constant worst-case memory or rare-history conditional guarantee. Exact linear predictive Hankel rank is infinite for the stationary scalar count process. Binary nonempty bins destroy the finite Poisson-times-Bernoulli class. No port-sensitive/interferometric or general nonlinear quantum filter is proved.

body: Leijdekker–Spreij (2008), Papaspiliopoulos–Ruggiero (2014), and Kon Kam King et al. (2023) establish the CIR gamma-mixture/dual-filter ingredients. The scoped reusable operation is the positive Poisson-times-real-root factorization with root interlacing, lifetime tags, an explicitly paid mean-preserving reset, and the resulting joint-law/expected-memory bounds. The independent check derives the key inequalities from the displayed equations. No external correctness, novelty, or complete finite-bit implementation claim follows.

review.scope: Acquired positive gamma-root update, real-root interlacing/lifetimes and paid mean-preserving reset under the supplied CIR/thermal/fine-count interface. Finite-horizon joint-law and summable anytime record-law bounds count expected real parameters, not worst-case bits or arbitrary policy memory. No port-sensitive closure or outward multi-bin implementation certificate.
